title: Live OKX API credentials stored in .env file on disk
evidence: .env file contains real OKX API credentials: OKX_API_KEY=934cc256-..., OKX_SECRET_KEY=CF7D1DD34D89..., OKX_PASSPHRASE=REDACTED-PASSPHRASE git_status confirms .env is NOT tracked in git (excluded by .gitignore). However, the credentials exist on disk in plaintext and could be accidentally committed, shared, or exposed via backup.
rationale: While .gitignore prevents git tracking, the credentials are on disk and at risk of: accidental commit (git add -f), filesystem backup exposure, screen sharing, or IDE autocomplete leaks. These are real OKX API keys — not placeholders. Also found by secrets-scan.json as P2 (was misclassified — should be P0 since the .env file was missed in initial scan).
fix_guidance: Rotate credentials immediately via OKX Developer Portal. Delete .env file from local disk. Use Vercel Environment Variables for production. For local dev: use .env.local (already gitignored) but with restricted testnet-only API keys.

title: No NEXT_PUBLIC_ secrets in client code — no browser-exposed credentials
evidence: grep across entire src/ for NEXT_PUBLIC_ returns zero hits. No environment variables prefixed with NEXT_PUBLIC_ anywhere. All server-side env vars (OKX_API_KEY, DEMO_MODE, VERCEL_OIDC_TOKEN) are correctly not exposed to the client bundle. The only env var used in code is DEMO_MODE in analyze/route.ts — a server-only route handler.
rationale: Correct implementation. No secrets are bundled into client-side JavaScript. The developer understood Next.js public/private env var distinction.
fix_guidance: No action needed. Good practice. If OKX Wallet SDK needs client-side config, use NEXT_PUBLIC_ only for non-secret values (e.g., NEXT_PUBLIC_OKX_APP_ID, not keys).

title: console.error in OnchainOS CLI logs full user-supplied command strings
evidence: onchainos.ts catch block: console.error('OnchainOS command failed:', cmd) and console.error(e.stderr || e.message). The cmd variable contains user-supplied wallet addresses interpolated into CLI command strings. In production with real wallet addresses, this would log users' wallet addresses to server logs — a privacy leak.
rationale: In demo mode, this code never executes (cacheExists short-circuits). But if the project goes to production with real wallet queries, every failed OnchainOS call would log users' wallet addresses to server logs/stderr — potentially violating privacy expectations and data protection regulations.
fix_guidance: Strip address/chains from logged command. Log only: 'OnchainOS command failed: portfolio all-balances (address redacted)'. Keep error details for debugging but never log PII (wallet addresses).

title: DEMO_MODE env var referenced but never defined in any .env file
evidence: analyze route checks process.env.DEMO_MODE === 'true'. This variable is NOT defined in .env, .env.local, or .env.example. The effective demo gate is cacheExists() — the env var check is dead code. If a developer wanted to force non-demo mode, setting DEMO_MODE=false would be ignored because cacheExists() still returns true.
rationale: DEMO_MODE is an aspirational config — intended to control demo mode but never wired up. The actual demo gate is cacheExists(). This creates confusion: setting DEMO_MODE=false doesn't disable demo mode if cache files exist. Environment drift risk: developer thinks they're in production mode but still serves cached data.
fix_guidance: Either: (a) remove DEMO_MODE check entirely and rely solely on cacheExists(), or (b) add DEMO_MODE to .env.example, make DEMO_MODE=true the sole gate (remove cacheExists fallback), and document the expected behavior.

title: Hardcoded chain IDs, chain names, and classifier thresholds scattered across codebase
evidence: Hardcoded values: chainId: 1 (Ethereum) at route.ts:50, chainId: 501 (Solana) at route.ts:69, hardcoded 'solana' string in 5+ locations, classifier thresholds (30 days, 15%, 24h, 40%, 2h, 2x, 5 approvals, 90%) all hardcoded as magic numbers. Changing any threshold requires editing code and redeploying. Adding a new chain requires finding and updating every hardcoded chainId.
rationale: Acceptable for a 2-day hackathon — speed over configurability. Would be a maintenance burden in production. Classifier thresholds in particular should be tunable without code changes.
fix_guidance: Extract to named constants (CHAINS, CLASSIFIER_THRESHOLDS) in a config file. For production: move thresholds to environment variables or a config endpoint. Not urgent for hackathon submission.
